Commentary.Commentary: There is still plenty in this wicket for the pace bowlers. The Bangla bowlers were extracting some movement with the new ball but their lines and lengths weren't accurate enough to pose any threat. The big West Indian bowlers will be raring to have another shot at the Bangladesh batting. Don't go anywhere as the action will get underway soon.

The Bangladesh bowlers woke up quite late in this Test match. The batting faltered miserably and their bowlers also failed to create any magic. It took them three sessions to realize their strength but the damage was already done by then. In the afternoon session today, they bagged quite a few wickets all thanks to their spinners while debutant Abu Jayed finished with a 3-wicket haul and was the only pacer to impress.

Outstanding batting performance by Windies. Kemar Roach set it up nicely for them yesterday morning and their batsmen just capitalized. They carried the momentum into their batting and went on to earn a massive first innings lead. Kraigg Brathwaite was the hero with the bat as he scored a gritty century and was also involved in three handy partnerships. Devon Smith, Kieran Powell and Shai Hope also lent good support while Jason Holder and Kemar Roach scored some quick runs towards the end.

He serves it on a fuller length around off and Shannon tries to heave it across the line over mid-wicket. But it takes the top edge of his bat and balloons in the air towards cover-point. Shakib Al Hasan settles underneath it and takes the skier safely. Right then, the innings ends with Bangladesh trailing by 363 runs.

Windies lead by 357 runs and the declaration has not come even now.

Comes from 'round the wicket for the left-hander and serves a flighted delivery. It's very full on middle and Cummins digs it out back to the bowler.
Full and flighted on off, driven down the ground to long off for a single.
Drifting into the batsman around off, once again it's been kept out from the crease to the off side.

Angling away from the batsman, on a good length, Cummins covers his stumps and lets it be.

Welcome back for the final session. 31 overs left in the day. How long can or will the Windies bat? Declare at 400 or keep Bangladesh further in the sun for as long as possible? The players are back on. And we shall have pace to start off the third session. Abu Jayed steaming in to Kemar Roach.
... DAY 2, FINAL SESSION ...

Can this Test match end today? Surely Bangladesh are a better team than what they displayed in the first session yesterday. They should be batting at some point of time in this first hour after Tea itself, but they need to keep their spirits high. Stay tuned...

In spite of all this, Bangladesh would be frustrated. They would have hoped to skittle out their opposition quickly after Holder's dismissal but Roach has come in and deflated them. He did it yesterday with the ball, taking 5 wickets in the space of 12 deliveries while now, he has come out all guns blazing, scoring 25 from 32 balls in an unbeaten partnership of 37 with Shai Hope.

Finally Bangladesh work on their strength - SPIN. Shakib struck in the very first over after the break to get the centurion Brathwaite and that helped open a door. The middle order did not last long and the hosts slipped from 272/3 to 288/6. Skipper Holder then came and played a counter-attacking knock before he was consumed by Mehidy.

End of a breezy knock by the Windies skipper. The lead is now five short of 300! Meanwhile, Mehidy Hasan has reached a landmark. Double switch here. Mehidy Hasan returns from the other end.
50-run stand comes up, off just 69 balls! Shortish and outside off, Holder punches it to deep cover for one. Retains strike. Windies lead by 295 runs.

Drinks break. The best hour in West Indies for Bangladesh. It accounted for three wickets and their spinners have looked quite deadly. All too late though. Windies have swelled their lead to 271 and with four wickets left, they might change their approach to play aggressive cricket now. A lead beyond 300 will be their first goal. Let's see what happens in the next half of this session.

OUT! That is a fantastic catch! Boy, the spinners are making merry now. Shakib has his second. He tosses this one outside off and Dowrich gets a long stride to defend. Now, to the naked eye, it seems like the ball has bounced and gone to silly point. But the bowler and fielder are pumped up and confident and the two umpires have a chat. After a long talk, the decision is referred upstairs but the soft signal is not out. Now, here come the replays. At least for us, the first angle itself is very clear. The ball goes off the bat, straight onto the boot and then towards silly point where Liton Das dives to his right and takes it one-handed! Multiple views are seen and eventually, the third umpire is convinced. Dowrich walks back shaking his head. The hosts have lost 17/3 in 8.3 overs post Lunch.
Howzzat? Well, Bangladesh seem confident about something. Shakib reckons that Dowrich has been caught at silly point. The soft signal is not out though...
